title: Perturb-seq reveals TCF7 as a transcriptional link between MAPK- and Wnt-driven gene expression.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and fully parsed GSE250558_all_results_combined.tsv.gz (113 MB compressed): exactly 3,223,427 rows, 10 columns (gene name, pval, adj_pval, F statistic, df1, df2, lfc, time, guide, index), 11,983 unique genes, 24 perturbation groups (22 transcription factors plus a SAFE cutting control and the RAF1 transgene), 3 time points (6/12/18 h), 4 individual guide RNAs per target, zero missing values, zero duplicate (gene, target, time, guide) keys. Counted significant results: only 8,654 rows and 3,630 unique (target, gene) pairs at adjusted p<0.05, of which 2,777 belong to the RAF1 transgene control; the 22 real transcription factors contribute ~850 pairs, concentrated in EGR1 (394), FOS (156), JUNB (73) and TCF7 (59). Measured guide-to-guide reproducibility of the log2 fold change label: Pearson 0.07-0.10 between any two guides of the same factor (n=560k-735k shared gene-target-time cells), and 0.07-0.31 when averaging two guides versus the other two (EGR1 best at 0.31). Also opened the CRISPR guide reference (112 guides, 25 target groups, with Ensembl gene identifiers) and two per-cell guide-assignment files (18,170 and 14,862 cells; 9,803 and 10,448 cells carried exactly one guide; 200-650 cells per factor per sample). Listed all GEO file manifests (GSE250559 superseries, 182 samples) and opened GSE333674_counts.tsv.gz (78,899 gene rows x 15 bulk samples).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That lfc is a log2 fold change relative to non-target control cells, computed on pseudobulk counts with glmGamPoi (a negative-binomial regression package) - the deposited table itself carries no data dictionary or units row. Also from text only: median 75-89 analysable cells per guide RNA, ~10,000 single-guide cells per sample, the 140-gene targeted (TAP-seq) panel, and the Zenodo deposit's contents (the Zenodo file listing would not load; only title, open-access status and description were retrievable).

a1_downloadable.note: Open GEO FTP, no login. Downloaded the 113 MB results table and several smaller files directly; Zenodo record 20486852 is marked open access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified in the file: 'lfc' (log2 fold change) and 'adj_pval' are literal columns, one row per gene x perturbed transcription factor x time x guide. No construction needed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Only identifiers are present (gene symbols in the results table, Ensembl gene IDs in the guide reference). Any sequence or motif features would come from one bulk Ensembl download, not thousands of lookups, so this passes but the file alone has no features.

a4_units_stated.note: Quantity is a log2 fold change, but the base is stated only in the paper's figure legends, not in the file; 45,760 rows (1.4%) have |lfc|>5 and the range runs to -70 and +37, i.e. degenerate regression fits on near-zero-count genes that need a filtering policy.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fails as effective sample size. 3.2M rows, but the unit of generalisation is the perturbed transcription factor: n=22, and only 4 of them (EGR1, FOS, JUNB, TCF7) have more than 27 significant target genes. Total positives across all 22 factors are ~850 unique (factor, gene) pairs. Worse, the label is noise-dominated: two guide RNAs targeting the same factor agree on the per-gene log2 fold change at Pearson 0.07-0.10, and 0.07-0.31 even after averaging pairs of guides. With 75-89 cells per guide, the measurement itself sets a ceiling near r=0.2, so neither training nor honest benchmarking is possible.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 113 MB compressed / ~0.8 GB in pandas for the results table; ~1 GB more if per-cell h5 matrices are added
a6_fits_laptop.note: Verified: the full table loaded in one pandas DataFrame at 0.77 GB. Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified agreement: paper claims 22 transcription factors, 3 time points, duplicates; the file has exactly 22 factor groups plus SAFE and RAF1-transgene controls, 3 time points, 4 guide indices, and 11,983 genes consistent with the untargeted library.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label traces to a physical measurement: unique molecular identifier counts from 10x single-cell RNA sequencing, summed to pseudobulk per guide and fitted with a negative-binomial regression (glmGamPoi). It is a statistical estimate, not another machine-learning model's output.

existing_models.name: GEARS (graph-enhanced gene activation and repression simulator, Nature Biotechnology 2023/2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported gains on held-out single and combinatorial perturbations in Perturb-seq data, with perturbation-level splits; later independent benchmarks did not reproduce an advantage over linear baselines.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to perturbations of genes never seen in training, and to new cell contexts.

existing_models.name: scGPT (single-cell foundation model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Claims perturbation-response prediction; in the 2025 benchmarks it did not beat a training-mean baseline on unseen perturbations.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer across cell types and to unseen perturbations.

existing_models.name: Ahlmann-Eltze, Huber & Anders benchmark, 'Deep-learning-based gene perturbation effect prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines' (Nature Methods 2025, 22:1657-1661)
existing_models.score_and_split: Compared five foundation models and two other deep models with deliberately simple baselines; none beat them. For unseen perturbations nothing beat 'predict the mean of the training perturbations'; for gene pairs nothing beat an additive model. Code and data on Zenodo.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Whether any current model extracts perturbation-specific signal at all beyond the dataset mean; they call for better evaluation.

existing_models.name: scPerturBench (Nature Methods 2025) and PerturBench (arXiv 2024), plus Systema (Nature Biotechnology 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: 27 methods across 29 datasets (scPerturBench) and 13 methods across 25 datasets (companion benchmark), evaluated on unseen single perturbations, combinations and cross-cell-type transfer with perturbation-level splits.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-cell-type and cross-context generalisation; metric calibration.

backbone.name: Not assessed beyond feasibility: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome models) would match the per-cell data, and AlphaGenome or DNABERT-2 (DNA sequence models) would match a promoter-sequence framing.
backbone.hardware: 16 GB laptop CPU would suffice for the table; per-cell embedding would want a GPU.
backbone.licence: Not checked - project rejected at Part A.

integration.partner_dataset: Replogle et al. 2022 genome-scale Perturb-seq (K562 and RPE1, >2.5M cells, 9,867 genes targeted) and the ENCODE/ChIP-Atlas transcription-factor binding catalogues.
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene identifier / HGNC gene symbol (both present: symbols in the results table, Ensembl IDs in the guide reference).
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the transcription-factor-to-target edges learned from large CRISPR interference screens in leukaemia cells predict the same factors' targets in a different cell line under acute MAPK pathway activation? - a good question, but this dataset's 22 factors and near-zero guide reproducibility cannot answer it.

controls.positive_control: Available and already demonstrated in the paper: knocking out the RAF1 transgene abolishes induction of the bulk-RNA-seq-defined MAPK target genes, and it is by far the strongest signal in the file (2,777 of 3,630 significant pairs).
controls.negative_control: Available: 10 non-targeting guides and 10 'safe cutter' guides are present as separate groups in the per-cell files and as the SAFE group in the results table.
controls.external_validation: Partly available: GSE250532 (EGR1/FOS knockout clones, 140 bulk samples) and GSE333674 (TCF7 knockout, 15 bulk samples) are independent bulk experiments on the same hypotheses, and GSE209899 is a re-used external EGR1-overexpression dataset.

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained here could only claim to rank genes by their response to one of 22 immediate-early transcription factors, in one engineered HEK293 cell line, 6-18 hours after artificial RAF1 activation, against a label whose own replicate guides agree at r=0.1 - so the claim could not be distinguished from fitting noise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a transcription factor's identity and a gene's promoter to predict how much that gene changes when the factor is knocked out.
plain_idea.train_on: One long table of 3,223,427 verified rows: for each of 11,983 genes, each of 22 transcription factors (plus two controls), 3 time points and 4 separate guide RNAs, the measured change in that gene's expression. Features would be the factor's identity plus gene-level features joined in from outside (promoter sequence, binding motifs, baseline expression).
plain_idea.predict: The log2 fold change of each gene's expression after the factor is knocked out, or the yes/no call of whether it is a significant target. The true answer comes from CRISPR Perturb-seq: single-cell RNA sequencing of cells carrying each guide, summed to pseudobulk and compared with non-targeting controls by negative-binomial regression.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups mapping signalling-to-transcription wiring (and the perturbation-prediction model community) would like a rule that says which genes a given factor controls without running a screen. Even a failure would quantify how much of a small Perturb-seq screen is reproducible signal.

more_or_better_data.why: Our 22 perturbations in one cell line are dwarfed by the public Replogle 2022 Perturb-seq screens (9,867 genes targeted in K562, >2.5M cells) that the existing models already train on, and by the 25-29 datasets in the 2025 benchmarks.

confidence_score.why: Four independent guide RNAs per factor plus two replicates do let you estimate noise, and I measured it (guide-to-guide Pearson 0.07-0.10) - but the estimate shows the label is mostly noise, which is a reason not to model it rather than an edge.

models_beatable.why: The relevant 2025 work is a set of honest benchmarks (Nature Methods 22:1657, scPerturBench, Systema) with perturbation-level held-out splits that already show deep models losing to a training-mean baseline; there is no published number on this dataset to beat and no weak incumbent to displace.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on the measurement condition: this screen's pseudobulk log2 fold changes from 75-89 cells per guide are not the same quantity measured the same way as the CRISPR interference screens the baselines use, and the evaluation split cannot be matched because only 22 perturbations exist.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict the per-gene log2 fold change (or the significant-target yes/no call) following knockout of each of 22 MAPK-induced transcription factors, from factor identity plus promoter sequence or motif features, with factors held out; and the alternative framing of using the table as an external validation set for GEARS/scGPT-style perturbation-response models. Both die on effective sample size (22 perturbations, 4 informative) and on a label whose replicate guide RNAs agree at Pearson 0.07-0.10, which makes a negative benchmark result uninterpretable.

effort.compute_note: Timed in practice: the 113 MB gzipped table downloaded in ~6 minutes from the GEO FTP mirror and loaded into pandas at 0.77 GB; the reproducibility and hit-count analysis ran in under 5 minutes on CPU. Embedding and cross-validation times not estimated because the project was rejected before modelling.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: The one I ran, in about 10 minutes: pivot the lfc column by guide index within each (factor, gene, time) and correlate guide 1-2 against guide 3-4. It returned 0.07-0.31, so the label's own replicates barely agree - do this before anything else on any small Perturb-seq screen.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 as effective sample size and label reliability. The file is genuinely clean and model-ready (3,223,427 rows, no missing values, no duplicates, label in a column, controls included), but the unit of generalisation is the perturbed transcription factor and there are only 22, of which just EGR1, FOS, JUNB and TCF7 have more than 27 significant targets; across all 22 there are ~850 significant (factor, gene) pairs versus 2,777 for the RAF1 transgene positive control. Decisively, I measured the noise ceiling myself: two guide RNAs against the same factor agree on the per-gene log2 fold change at Pearson 0.07-0.10 (0.07-0.31 after averaging guide pairs), because each estimate rests on 75-89 cells. That caps any achievable correlation near 0.2 and makes both training and honest benchmarking impossible. The field is also saturated with open, honestly evaluated models and 2025 benchmarks (GEARS, scGPT, scPerturBench, Systema, Nature Methods 22:1657) run on far larger screens, so even a clean result here would add nothing. The paper's own biology (the EGR1-TCF7 feedback loop) is well supported by its orthogonal bulk experiments; it is just not an ML dataset.
